newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese airline pilots begin 48-hour strike.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese airline pilots begin 48-hour strike.

text.p: Pilots of loss-making state airline TAP Air-Portugal began a 48-hour strike on Thursday after last-minute talks with the company failed to end a dispute over working hours.
The company's 430 pilots will ground all flights except those linking Portugal with its Atlantic Azores and Madeira islands.
TAP has been pressing for more flexible working hours but the pilots say that they already fly more hours than colleagues with other European airlines.
The airline, which lost 10.5 billion escudos last year, has warned that the pilot's action could jeopardise its chances of making a profit this year for the first time since 1974.

The Socialist government says that it plans to privatise the airline in 1998 but without changes to regulations on working hours, TAP says it will not be able to find the strategic partner it needs to survive in an increasingly competitive airline industry.
